paths.description: Homepage and directory entry point; covers primary navigation, featured/latest listings, preferences, performance, security, and mobile layout.
Telugu featured category, representative of listing/archive templates.
Representative movie detail page; covers entity metadata, content layout, and listing-to-detail journey.
Primary search flow with query “Lenin”; selected because search is the main task affordance.
Unknown route used to assess HTTP/error recovery behavior.

findings.summary: Theme is fixed rather than preference-driven
findings.evidence: The normal and prefers-color-scheme: dark screenshots are pixel-identical, and the CSS probe found no prefers-color-scheme or color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `color-scheme: light dark` and preference-driven surface tokens using `light-dark()` or a prefers-color-scheme query.

findings.summary: No high-contrast or forced-colors adaptation
findings.evidence: The stylesheet probe found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors rule; controls and gray-on-dark chrome rely on fixed authored colors.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast adaptations, preserving visible focus, borders, and system colors.

findings.summary: Route changes are abrupt
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found no `view-transition-name`, `@view-transition`, or transition navigation handling across the listing and detail templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Use cross-document View Transitions for same-origin listing-to-detail navigation, with a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Navigation chrome does not react to scroll state
findings.evidence: The page is 7,383 CSS pixels tall on mobile, but DOM/CSS inspection found no scroll-state query or progress/current-position affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a sticky, scroll-state-aware compact header or lightweight progress affordance where it helps long listings.

findings.summary: Hover menus use brittle absolute positioning
findings.evidence: Submenus are `position:absolute; top:37px; left:0` and shown only through `li:hover`; there is no anchor positioning or fallback placement.
findings.suggestedFix: Use popover plus CSS anchor positioning and `position-try`, while retaining a keyboard/touch fallback.

findings.summary: A transparent full-page advertising layer intercepts the page
findings.evidence: The live probe found `#dontfoid` fixed at 780×493 with z-index 2147483647 over the viewport; Lighthouse found the equivalent full-page link in the tab order with no name.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the click-capture ad layer. Ads must be visible, clearly identified, non-blocking, and never intercept unrelated page actions.

findings.summary: The advertising overlay is an ad-hoc, non-dismissible div/link
findings.evidence: The overlay probe found zero dialog, popover, or details elements but did find a viewport-sized fixed `#dontfoid` layer with no visible dismiss control.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the overlay; if a legitimate transient surface is needed, use a semantic popover/dialog with explicit and light-dismiss behavior.

findings.summary: Dense navigation and sidebar compete with content
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshots show a wide multi-level nav and sidebar squeezing/clipping the primary movie content; the first viewport devotes substantial area to chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Simplify top-level categories, move secondary filters into a disclosure/drawer, and prioritize the listing/detail content.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior is viewport-only
findings.evidence: The stylesheet contains many viewport media queries and fixed template widths but no `@container` or `container-type` rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Use container queries for reusable movie cards, sidebars, and navigation components while retaining viewport fallbacks.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is suppressed on primary navigation
findings.evidence: The focus probe reports `outline: none 0px` and no text decoration for Home, Featured, and other top-level links; hidden submenu links can also receive focus at 0×0.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a strong `:focus-visible` ring and ensure collapsed submenu items are removed from sequential focus until opened.

findings.summary: The primary search flow is blocked by a security challenge
findings.evidence: A direct search for “Lenin” returned HTTP 403 and rendered an indefinite Cloudflare “Performing security verification” screen instead of results.
findings.suggestedFix: Tune bot protection so normal search navigation succeeds, and provide a bounded, accessible error/retry path when verification cannot complete.

findings.summary: Parser-loaded ad scripts and a redirect add avoidable network work
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 51 requests and 597 KB transferred; parser-inserted `aclib.js` is not async/defer, and the requested host redirects to a different domain.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the intrusive ad scripts, consolidate the canonical host, and defer non-critical third-party code.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts dominate transferred JavaScript
findings.evidence: HAR shows Google Tag Manager at 165,869 bytes plus 66,844 bytes from acscdn scripts, despite a mostly static server-rendered page.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the ad network code and load only analytics needed for a declared purpose, after consent where required.

findings.summary: The injected full-page link has no accessible name
findings.evidence: Lighthouse `link-name` failed on `body > a#dontfoid`: it is in the tab order, covers the viewport, and has no text or ARIA name.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the injected link; all remaining links must have a visible, descriptive accessible name.

findings.summary: Focus and list semantics are broken
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports sidebar `li` elements outside a semantic list, while the focus probe found invisible 0×0 submenu links and no visible outline on primary navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Repair list markup and implement disclosure-based submenus with managed expanded state and visible focus.

findings.summary: Poster images are distorted and undersized
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports displayed 176×200 posters with intrinsic 165×220 ratios, and low-resolution sources for the rendered size.
findings.suggestedFix: Preserve intrinsic aspect ratio with `height:auto`/`aspect-ratio` and provide correctly sized responsive sources.

findings.summary: Indexing signals are internally inconsistent
findings.evidence: The requested `.house` URL redirects to `.vote`; `/sitemap.xml` returns 404, and the custom 404 document declares `index,follow` plus a self-canonical URL.
findings.suggestedFix: Choose one canonical host, publish a sitemap, and send `noindex` on error pages while retaining the real HTTP 404 status.

findings.summary: Movie entities lack structured data
findings.evidence: The homepage has Open Graph tags, but the probe found zero JSON-LD blocks; the audited movie detail template likewise exposes no machine-readable Movie entity.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org Movie JSON-LD and page-specific Open Graph metadata matching visible title, image, synopsis, cast, and language.

findings.summary: Core security headers are missing
findings.evidence: Headers evidence confirms HTTPS but no CSP, HSTS, or X-Content-Type-Options; only X-Frame-Options is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrictive CSP, HSTS, and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`; migrate inline scripts so the CSP does not require unsafe-inline.

findings.summary: Tracking and advertising run without a visible consent choice
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found seven third-party origins including Google Analytics, acscdn, adexchangerapid, and usrpubtrk; HAR attributes 596,755 of 597,148 transferred bytes to non-requested origins because of the cross-host redirect and third parties.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove opaque ad/tracking vendors, minimize analytics, document purpose, and gate non-essential collection behind an informed choice.

findings.summary: Defensive browser policies are incomplete
findings.evidence: No CSP, HSTS, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or nosniff header was present; clickjacking is the only covered policy via SAMEORIGIN.
findings.suggestedFix: Set CSP (including frame-ancestors), HSTS, nosniff, a strict Referrer-Policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Search falls into an indefinite verification state
findings.evidence: The search route rendered a Cloudflare verification screen and returned 403, with no site navigation, timeout, or recovery action.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a resilient server-rendered results path and a clear timeout/retry/back route if verification fails.

findings.summary: The search failure state has no recovery
findings.evidence: The custom 404 correctly offers “Return to home,” but a 403 search response only shows an indefinite third-party verification spinner.
findings.suggestedFix: Handle 403/timeouts as first-party error states with an explanation, retry, home navigation, and preserved query.

findings.summary: The page disguises an advertisement as the whole page
findings.evidence: A transparent viewport-sized `#dontfoid` layer with maximum z-index captures clicks while the visible page appears normal, a disguised-ad interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove disguised click interception. Commercial links must be visible, labelled, and activated only by the control the user intentionally chose.

findings.summary: All poster images use legacy, non-responsive delivery
findings.evidence: The image audit found 32/32 JPGs, 32/32 without srcset, and 28 below-fold images without lazy loading.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants, add width-based srcset/sizes, and lazy-load below-fold posters.

findings.summary: Background analytics and ad requests are disproportionate
findings.evidence: The mostly static page makes eight analytics requests plus ad-network requests; third-party scripts account for over 230 KB of JavaScript transfer.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the ad network and batch/minimize analytics so idle page viewing does not trigger unnecessary background work.

findings.summary: Third-party advertising consumes a large share of the page budget
findings.evidence: HAR and tracker evidence identify GTM plus two ad/tracking networks; JavaScript transfer is 233,766 bytes and 49 of 51 requests are classified away from the requested origin.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt a third-party budget, eliminate the click-capture vendor, consolidate hosts, and defer any retained analytics.
